findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, http, extract, x402_check, bazaar_check, market_quote, screenshot, search, pdf, money_market_rates · Private data: portfolio, fetch, http, extract, bazaar_check, screenshot · Public sink: http, extract, x402_check, market_quote, money_market_rates · Destructive: fetch, http, screenshot.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, http, extract, x402_check, bazaar_check, market_quote, screenshot, search, pdf, money_market_rates · Private data: portfolio, fetch, http, extract, bazaar_check, screenshot · Public sink: http, extract, x402_check, market_quote, money_market_rates · Destructive: fetch, http, screenshot

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
